_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 11: RSS (id 'rss')
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote; DERIVED = arithmetic done here; EFFECTIVE = none used; INFERRED = a reading not stated; MEASURED = read from a figure with a stated scale; NOT FOUND = gap.
_meta.status: in operation; detector replaced in 2026 (preset = 2011-2026-1 three-CCD era); no '(design)' tag

rss.title: SALT RSS: all-refractive prime-focus imaging spectrograph, F/4.2 feed on the 11 m SAC pupil, 150 mm beam (f 630 mm), F/2.2 articulating camera (330 mm), VPH gratings 900-3000 /mm, 3 x E2V 44-82 CCDs
rss.aperture_handling: D = 11 m (SAC pupil defining F/4.2); the illuminated pupil varies with the track (effective area of a 7-9 m telescope, default 46 m^2); R independent of D; note overstates area by 2.1

parameters.parameter: Design pupil and focal ratio at the RSS focus
parameters.value: 11 m pupil at F/4.2; 8 arcmin field
parameters.quote: uses the SAC specification for an 11m telescope pupil at F/4.2, and an eight arcmin field of view | ALT WOV Sec. 2.1: The Spherical Aberration Corrector (SAC) delivers a F/4.2 beam providing a flat, 8 arcminute diameter field of view at the focal plane
parameters.note: The corrector (SAC) feeds RSS at the prime focus. The 11 m figure is the SAC design pupil, not the pupil that is illuminated at any moment (see the next row).

parameters.quote: SAC specification for an 11m telescope pupil at F/4.2 | ALT WOV Sec. 2.1: with a plate scale of 4.5 arcsec/mm
parameters.note: DERIVED: 4.2 x 11 000 mm = 46 200 mm; plate scale 206 265 / 46 200 = 4.465 arcsec/mm (published 4.5, 0.8% higher).

parameters.parameter: Entrance pupil distance from the focal plane
parameters.quote: the entrance pupil is 586 mm from the focal plane
parameters.note: Why the collimator opens with a strong field lens.

parameters.parameter: Illuminated pupil varies with the track
parameters.value: effective area equivalent to a 7 to 9 m telescope; simulator default 46 m^2
parameters.quote: SALT is equivalent to between a ~7 to 9 m diameter conventional telescope depending on the pupil | ALT CALL Sec. 4.4: The current default collecting area in the instrument Simulators is set to 46 m
parameters.note: HANDLING: as for HET (data/round9/hpf.md). The preset keeps D = 11 m, the SAC pupil that defines F/4.2 and the 150 mm beam; the resolving power does not depend on D (R is set by the slit, f_col/f_cam and the grating angle; the diffraction limit is >1e5), so D enters only the arcsec bookkeeping and any collecting-area estimate. A flux or S/N estimate with D = 11 m overstates the collecting area: the default is 46 m^2 (CALL), against pi/4 x 11^2 = 95 m^2, a factor 2.1; the note must say so. Absolute spectrophotometry is not possible on SALT.

parameters.quote: 0.60 arcsec wide x 8 arcmin long | ALT WSP Sec. 3.2.2: 2.00 arcsec wide x 8 arcmin long
parameters.note: Original (UW) complement; the current list is in the SALT PIPT. Table 7.2 of the current call quotes R for a 1.25 arcsec slit and the SMI paper 1.5 arcsec, so the PIPT list differs.

parameters.quote: 0.90 arcsec wide x 8 arcmin long
parameters.note: The 8 arcmin science field. DERIVED along the slit: 480 arcsec / 0.1267 arcsec per pixel = 3790 px across the 4096-px short axis.

parameters.value: 10 tilted long slits; 30 MOS masks; up to ~40 objects per mask
parameters.quote: slit-mask magazine has room for ten tilted longslits | ALT CALL Sec. 7.3: of up to ~40 objects at a time | ALT CALL Sec. A.7: The magazine can carry 30 of these customised slitmasks
parameters.note: nObj: 1 for the long-slit preset; ~40 is the MOS capacity.

parameters.value: refractive: 9 lenses in 5 groups with a fold mirror before the last doublet
parameters.quote: The collimator has 9 lenses in 5 groups plus a fold mirror before the last doublet | ALT OD Sec. 3.5: The final element in the visible beam collimator is a CaF2/ fused silica doublet
parameters.note: Materials: fused silica, fused quartz, CaF2 and NaCl only (OD Sec. 2.2: The current model uses only fused silica, fused quartz, CaF2, and NaCl). All-transmissive: OD Sec. 2.2 'All- transmission optics for high efficiency and compactness'.

parameters.value: ON-AXIS lens train (no obscuration, no slit in a returning beam); one 90 deg fold in the last part of the collimator
parameters.quote: All- transmission optics for high efficiency and compactness | ALT OD Sec. 3.5: starts with a doublet field lens, fused quartz/ CaF2, placed close to the focal plane
parameters.note: VERDICT (deploy gate): a transmissive collimator has no obscuration and no returning beam; the slit sits at the focal plane in front of the field lens. colTilt 0 and col 'lens'. The fold turns the beam 90 deg (45 deg flat; MEASURED, Fig. 2 side view: the collimator axis is vertical, the camera axis horizontal).

parameters.quote: In the 150 mm diameter collimated beam are the shutter and the dispersers | ALT OD Sec. 2.2: Beam size 150 mm, the maximum for practical Fabry-Perot etalons
parameters.note: Set by the largest etalon available.

parameters.quote: High speed (F/4.2) | ALT OD Sec. 2.2: Beam size 150 mm
parameters.note: DERIVED: the F/4.2 beam of the 11 m pupil fills the 150 mm beam, so f_col = 4.2 x 150 = 630 mm. Not stated; the published plate scales confirm it (next rows).

parameters.quote: The fastest affordable refractive UV camera was judged to be F/2.2 | ALT OD Sec. 3.5: a perfect 330mm focal length camera | ALT CALL Sec. A.6: The camera (F/2.2, 8.6 arcsec/mm)
parameters.note: DERIVED: 2.2 x 150 = 330 mm, equal to the design focal length. DERIVED check: telescope-scale at the detector 46 200 x 330 / 630 = 24 200 mm, 206 265/24 200 = 8.52 arcsec/mm (published 8.6; 0.1267 arcsec/px at 15 um implies 8.447 arcsec/mm, 0.9% below 8.52 and 1.8% below 8.6). The explorer's 330 mm gives 0.1279 arcsec/px at the chip center (the printed 8.52 arcsec/mm x 15 um), 0.9% above the published 0.1267; a 333 mm camera would match it exactly, but 330 mm is the sourced value and the 0.9% is left as a stated miss.

parameters.value: refractive, 9 elements in 4 groups, one asphere (first surface), field flattener = dewar window; 16 deg field
parameters.quote: The PFIS design has 9 elements in 4 groups | ALT CALL Sec. A.6: with the final lens, a field flattener, being the dewar window | ALT OD Sec. 3.2: rather large camera field of view, 16
parameters.note: The camera tube (with the detector) articulates about the grating axis; its length is limited to < 625 mm (OD Sec. 3.2: The overall length was constrained to be < 625 mm).

parameters.value: VPH transmission grating in the 150 mm collimated beam at the pupil; the camera articulates about the grating axis
parameters.quote: The dispersors are located in the 150mm diameter, 350 mm long collimated beam | ALT CALL Sec. A.6: the entire camera articulates about the same axis as the grating rotation
parameters.note: VPH gratings are transmission gratings used in first order only (CALL Sec. 7.5: All gratings are used in first order only).

parameters.parameter: Distance, last collimator element to the exit pupil (grating)
parameters.quote: The exit pupil was constrained to be 360 mm from the last element of the collimator
parameters.note: The 2001 PDR version put the pupil 45 mm beyond the articulation axis (PDR Sec. 3.5). The grating stands at or near the pupil. layLen candidate (drawing only): 360 mm, with the thin collimator lens placed accordingly.

parameters.value: not published
parameters.quote: The overall length was constrained to be < 625 mm
parameters.note: Only the camera's length limit is published (< 625 mm, from the first camera element to the detector); the distance from the grating to the first camera element is NOT FOUND (the figures are unscaled).

parameters.section: Gratings (all VPH, fused silica, fringes normal to the surface)
parameters.value: PG0700 (off-Littrow), PG0900, PG1300, PG1800, PG2300, PG3000
parameters.quote: using the six available Littrow VPH gratings (PG700, PG900, PG1300, PG1800, PG2300, and PG3000, where the number refers to the line-density in mm | ALT VPH Sec. 2: 900 200 175 180 155
parameters.note: The original five (900, 1300, 1800, 2300, 3000) are in the 2003 VPH specification; PG0700 was added later and is used off-Littrow at 3.0-7.5 deg (CALL Table 7.2 and note [1]); the old ruled 300 /mm grating is no longer available for science (CALL Sec. 7.5).

parameters.section: Gratings (all VPH, fused silica, fringes normal to the surface)
parameters.parameter: VPH sizes and clear apertures along the dispersion
parameters.note: gLen candidates (the explorer's ruled length of the VPH along the dispersion). DERIVED: the 150 mm beam at 50 deg makes a 150 / cos 50 = 233 mm footprint, inside 237 mm; no overfill. Fringe tilt 0: Fringe tilt 0 (normal to surface), so the explorer's gTilt = 0.

parameters.section: Gratings (all VPH, fused silica, fringes normal to the surface)
parameters.parameter: Usable grating angles and bandpass per tilt
parameters.note: 'Usable angles' is the grating tilt alpha to the collimated beam.

parameters.section: Gratings (all VPH, fused silica, fringes normal to the surface)
parameters.parameter: Camera articulation = twice the grating angle
parameters.value: psi = 2 alpha (Littrow/Bragg setting); maximum articulation 100 deg
parameters.quote: The RSS camera is then articulated to twice the grating angle since the VPH efficiency curve for a given grating angle typically is at a maximum at the Littrow wavelength | ALT CALL Sec. A.6: with a maximum articulation of 100 degrees
parameters.note: For the explorer (psi = alpha - beta in the usual reflection convention, 0 at Littrow): a transmission VPH at its Bragg setting is entered as gType 'trans' with the symmetric incidence (tAlpha null); the explorer's deviation alpha + beta = 2 alpha is then the camera-collimator angle (S.psi), so no psi is entered. Camera angle = 2 x grating angle: 31.75 deg for 15.875, 42.25 for 21.125, 81.2 for 40.6, 100 for 50.

parameters.section: Gratings (all VPH, fused silica, fringes normal to the surface)
parameters.quote: the camera angle is quantized to every 0.75 degrees
parameters.note: CONFLICT: the 2003 articulation specification asked for 0.5 deg steps (ART: 0.5 degrees apart between 0 and 100 degrees of articulation) and the papers quote grating angles in steps of 0.125 deg (15.875, 21.125), so the grating angle itself is not a multiple of 0.75/2. Settings below use the quoted grating angles and psi = 2 alpha.

parameters.value: 3 x (2048 x 4102) pixels of 15 um; 0.1267 arcsec/pixel; readout in 2x2 binning typical
parameters.quote: The chips are E2V (formerly Marconi) 44-82 CCDs with 2k x 4k x 15 micron pixels | ALT CALL Sec. 7.3: The pixel scale of the RSS detector is 0.1267 arcseconds per unbinned pixel | ALT DET Sec. 8.3.1: ie. 4096+6 = 4102 pixels
parameters.note: The long axis (3 x 2048) lies along the dispersion (OD Sec. 3.1: with the long dimension in the dispersion direction).

parameters.value: about 1.5 mm each (about 100 px)
parameters.quote: The gap between packages is nominally 0.5mm | ALT DET Sec. 8.3.1: Left and right inactive edge spacing per CCD is nominally 0.5mm | ALT MAL Sec. 3: total size of 3171
parameters.note: DERIVED: 0.5 mm package gap + 0.5 mm inactive edge on each side = 1.5 mm = 100 px of 15 um between active areas (design values). Two gaps add 200 px to 6144: 6344 px across the mosaic. The MALS paper's 2x2-binned frame of 3171 px (= 6342 unbinned) agrees to 2 px (INFERRED: the 3171 includes the gaps). The explorer has no gaps: enter Nx = 6344 so that the wavelength span includes them, and say the gap columns carry no data.

parameters.value: 6k x 6k, 15 um pixels; 0.1267 arcsec/pixel (unchanged); no chip gaps; full frame 6160 rows
parameters.quote: The chip is the E2V 231-C6 CCD with 6k x 6k x 15 micron pixels | ALT CALL Sec. 7.4: The frame size of 6160 represents the full frame | ALT CALL Sec. 7.1: just no chip gaps
parameters.note: In 2026 the old three-CCD detector was replaced (call text: 2026-2 is shared-risk; the optics are not altered). Whether commissioning had finished by 2026-11-18 is not stated. The exact pixel count along the dispersion is NOT FOUND ('6k'): INFERRED 6144.

parameters.value: 320-900 nm (design)
parameters.quote: optimized for spectroscopic performance in the 320-900 nm wavelength range
parameters.note: The collimator is designed for 320-1700 nm (WOV Sec. 2.1.1); the NIR arm was built as a separate instrument (CALL Sec. A.6). Throughput below 400 nm is poor (CALL Sec. 7.8: PIs are warned that the RSS throughput below 400 nm is not nearly as good as expected originally).

parameters.quote: UV PC03200, PC03400, PC03850 | ALT CALL Sec. 7.6: Blue PC04600
parameters.note: In the filter magazine just before the detector (OD Sec. 3.2). Not entered in the explorer except as a note.

parameters.parameter: Resolving power vs grating (1.25 arcsec slit), design table
parameters.note: Range over the usable angles; not a measurement (Zemax-based for PG0700: CALL note [2]: Resolution estimated using Zemax model of the grating and a 1.5 slit).

parameters.parameter: Maximum resolving power at 1.25 and 0.6 arcsec
parameters.quote: 1.25 arcsec slit: 5300; 0.6 arcsec slit: 10000
parameters.note: GEOMETRIC design requirement at the maximum grating tilt of 50 deg (OD Sec. 2.2: R = (2 tan 2i / 2s) (d/D), the grating-tilt form with 2i the tilt). Later call text: R ~ 5000 with 1 arcsec slits and ~9000 with 0.6 arcsec slits (CALL Sec. 7.3: up to R ~ 5000 with 1 arcsec slits; R ~ 9000 with 0.6 arcsec slits).

parameters.parameter: Guideline resolving power at the central wavelength
parameters.note: The slit is not stated. INFERRED: the central wavelength is the Littrow wavelength 2 sin(alpha)/G at one tilt: PG0900 605 nm gives alpha = asin(0.605 x 0.9 / 2) = 15.8 deg (the 15.875 deg setting of MAL); PG2300 566 nm and PG3000 434 nm both give 40.6 deg.

parameters.value: coverage 4486-7533 A
parameters.quote: We used RSS PG0900 grating with a grating tilt angle of 15.875 | ALT MAL Sec. 3: of 4486-7533
parameters.note: Measured coverage, with gaps at 5497-5551 and 6542-6589 A (the chip gaps).

parameters.value: coverage 6445-9400 A; 4.8 A FWHM; 0.97 A/pixel
parameters.quote: With a grating angle of 21.125 degrees | ALT PGQ Sec. 2: at a spectral resolution of 4.8 | ALT PGQ Sec. 2: reciprocal dispersion of 0.97
parameters.note: Binning is not stated. The coverage 2955 A over the 6344-px mosaic gives 0.466 A/px unbinned (0.93 A/px binned 2x2), so 0.97 A/pixel is the 2x2 binned value (INFERRED).

parameters.parameter: PG3000, PG2300, PG0900 programs (2 arcsec slit, 2x2 binning)
parameters.quote: = 3409-4488 ... 1936, 2188 | ALT CAR Sec. 2: with a corresponding resolution element of 7.87 pixels
parameters.note: Two central wavelengths per grating (dither angles not given), so the grating angles are NOT FOUND and these R values are not used as tests. 2 arcsec / 0.1267 = 15.8 px unbinned = 7.9 px binned, consistent with 2x2 binning and 7.87 px.

parameters.value: < 0.4 arcsec RMS in the dispersion direction for field angles < 3 arcmin
parameters.quote: < 0.4 arcsec RMS width in dispersion direction for field angles < 3 arcmin
parameters.note: Optical image quality, a few percent of the 1.2 arcsec slit image; the model's geometric slit image has none, so it overstates R slightly for the narrowest slits.

parameters.value: 75-82% over the visible camera range, excluding the CCD, dispersers and polarimetric optics
parameters.quote: We expect the throughput to be in the 75-82% range across the entire visible camera wavelength range
parameters.note: A design prediction; measured end-to-end throughput is in graphs of the call (CALL Fig. 4.3), not text: NOT FOUND as a number.

recommended_presets.name: SALT / RSS PG0900 15.9°, 1.2″
recommended_presets.why: Most used setting: the PG0900 at 15.875 deg (MAL) is the setting behind the call's guideline R and central wavelength (605 nm, Table 7.8), the grating of most SALT programs (MOS surveys, transients, classification); covers Hbeta to Halpha.

recommended_presets.name: SALT / RSS PG0900 21.1°, 1.2″
recommended_presets.why: The red PG0900 setting with a published coverage (6445-9400 A), dispersion and FWHM (PGQ); an independent test of the geometry.

recommended_presets.name: SALT / RSS PG2300 40.6°, 1.2″
recommended_presets.why: Medium-high resolution for the Hbeta-[OIII]-Na D region at R ~ 4000; the angle is DERIVED from the call's Table 7.8 central wavelength (566 nm).

recommended_presets.name: SALT / RSS PG3000 50°, 1.2″
recommended_presets.why: The highest-resolution VPH at the maximum grating tilt (50 deg) and the maximum 100 deg articulation (the call's Fig. A.19 example); the FPRD's maximum-R requirement (R = 5300 at 1.25 arcsec) applies to this tilt.

new_detector_2026.note: INFERRED from '6k x 6k' and the 6160-row full frame; no gaps

validation.src: CALL Sec. 7.3; model 0.1279 at the center (+0.9%)
MAL Sec. 3; model 4522 (+0.8%); NOT fitted (Nx 6344 from the chip spacing)
PGQ Sec. 2; model 0.471 unbinned = 0.942 binned (-2.9%); binning INFERRED

PGQ Sec. 2; model dlamRes 5.53 A (+15%): the model's slit image is geometric, the measured arcs are narrower (the slit is imaged with design aberrations of < 0.4 arcsec RMS and the arc lamp fills the slit uniformly)

validation.what: R = 5300 at 1.25 arcsec, PG3000 50 deg (maximum tilt)

validation.src: CALL Table 7.2; model: PG0900 1280 at 15.9 deg, PG2300 3857 at 40.6 deg and 5363 at 50 deg (inside the ranges); R scales as tan(alpha) at fixed slit, a simpler law than the table's endpoints (PG1300 at 32 deg: model 2812 vs 3200)
CALL Table 7.8; slit not stated. Model at 1.25 arcsec: 1280 (+20%), 3857 (+20%), 3857 (+20%), the same +20% for all three if the slit were about 1.5 arcsec
